idiom_name: state-owning goroutine + intent channel + pure reduce(State, Intent) State + snapshot broadcast
implementation_notes: Go has no UI framework and no MVI library, so the loop is a small explicit type: intents are values sent on a channel to a single owning goroutine that applies a pure reduce(state, intent) and publishes an immutable snapshot, or the state is guarded by a sync.Mutex with the same reducer. The channel-ownership form is the Go-idiomatic reading of 'single source of truth' ('share memory by communicating') and serializes concurrent intents for free; maps and slices must still be cloned inside the reducer because Go copies are shallow. Hand-writing is justified for TUI programs, daemons and test harnesses whose shared state must be replayed or observed from several components; a request-scoped handler is simpler with a plain struct.
pitfalls: Value copies are shallow: a State holding a map or slice shares its backing storage with the previous snapshot, so writes corrupt history; clone before mutating.
Publishing to subscribers while holding the store lock deadlocks once a subscriber sends an intent; snapshot under the lock and publish after releasing it.
An unbounded intent channel or an ever-growing subscriber list leaks; bound the queue and tie subscriptions to a context.
Interface fields holding pointers inside State reintroduce aliasing; keep state fields as values or clone explicitly at the boundary.
